- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.8) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- After a price spike (e.g., >70), model often overshoots in the next 5–7 days; apply downward correction by 2–5% of the spike magnitude.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤ 0.2) within 3–5 days, model may lag in adjusting downward; anticipate a 1–3 day lag and adjust forecast downward by 1–3% per day.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price is above 75; model often overestimates; cap forecast at 75–78 unless sentiment strongly bullish.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.2–0.8), model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast by averaging last 5–7 days’ values.
- If model forecast is >75 and sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce forecast by 3–5% to avoid overbought bias.
- In low-sentiment periods (e.g., sentiment < 0.3 for 3+ days), model often underestimates; add 1–3% to forecast to account for hidden demand or policy surprises.
